# Medical Wound Healing Accelerator and Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to medical devices for promoting tissue healing, and more particularly, to a wound healing accelerator designed for use in conjunction with external fixation systems employed in fracture treatment, as well as a related device for the treatment of osteomyelitis.

## Background

In the treatment of complex fractures, external fixators are commonly employed to stabilize bone fragments during the healing process. These devices typically utilize fixing pins that are inserted percutaneously—passing through the skin and soft tissue and anchoring directly into the bone. While essential for fracture stabilization, the insertion sites of these fixing pins create open wounds at the point where the pin penetrates the skin. These pin-tract wounds are susceptible to delayed healing, inflammation, and infection, necessitating dedicated therapeutic intervention to support proper tissue recovery.

## Summary of the Invention

### Wound Healing Accelerator

The disclosed medical wound healing accelerator is specifically engineered to address the unique healing challenges presented at fixing pin insertion sites. The device comprises a body configured for detachable coupling to a fixing pin—the same pin that forms part of the external fixator apparatus and is inserted through the skin into the underlying bone structure. This attachable/detachable configuration allows the healing accelerator to be conveniently installed onto existing external fixator hardware without requiring modification to the fixator itself, and permits removal for maintenance, cleaning, or replacement as needed throughout the treatment period.

On one lateral surface of the body, a plurality of light source units is arranged in a distributed configuration. These light source units are oriented to emit therapeutic light directly onto the skin surface surrounding the fixing pin, targeting the wound site to deliver beneficial photobiomodulation effects. The therapeutic light emitted by these units is intended to promote cellular activity conducive to tissue repair, reduce inflammation, and support the overall healing process at the pin-skin interface—an area that is otherwise prone to complications due to continuous mechanical interaction with the fixator hardware and exposure to the external environment.

To ensure precise and effective delivery of the therapeutic light, a controller is electrically connected to the light source units. This controller governs the operational parameters of the light sources, including but not limited to activation timing, intensity, duration, and emission patterns. By regulating these parameters, the controller enables customized treatment protocols tailored to the specific healing requirements of individual patients, optimizing therapeutic outcomes while ensuring safe and consistent operation of the device.

### Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

In addition to the wound healing accelerator, the present disclosure further provides an osteomyelitis treatment device designed to address bone infections that may arise as a complication of fracture treatment or external fixation. This device includes an insertable component configured for placement at or near the site of osteomyelitis-affected bone tissue.

The insertable component features a plurality of light-emitting members arranged in a spaced-apart configuration along its length. Notably, this component is designed with adaptability in mind: it can be cut or bent as necessary to conform precisely to the particular anatomical shape and dimensions of the affected osteomyelitis region. This flexibility allows clinicians to customize the device's form factor at the point of care, ensuring optimal contact and light delivery to irregularly shaped or extensively affected bone areas that are characteristic of osteomyelitis presentations.

The spaced-apart arrangement of the light-emitting members further ensures that therapeutic light is distributed effectively across the treatment area, even after modification of the component's shape, thereby maintaining consistent therapeutic coverage regardless of how the device has been adapted for the specific clinical scenario.

## Advantages

The combination of these two complementary devices provides a comprehensive solution for addressing both superficial wound healing at fixator pin sites and deeper bone infection concerns, offering clinicians versatile tools to enhance patient outcomes throughout the course of fracture treatment and recovery.

# Medical Device for Targeted Light Therapy in Wound Healing and Osteomyelitis Treatment

## Background of the Invention

Wound healing complications and osteomyelitis (bone infection) represent significant challenges in orthopedic and trauma medicine, particularly in cases involving external fixation devices used to stabilize fractures. Traditional treatment approaches often struggle to deliver targeted therapeutic intervention directly at the site of injury or infection, especially when that site is located deep within tissue or bone structures. There exists a substantial need for medical devices capable of providing precise, adjustable therapeutic light delivery to accelerate healing processes and combat bacterial infection at these critical anatomical locations.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides an innovative medical device system designed to address the dual challenges of wound healing acceleration and osteomyelitis treatment through targeted phototherapy delivery mechanisms.

### First Embodiment: External Fixator-Compatible Light Therapy Device

In one aspect of the invention, a medical device is provided comprising a body structure specifically configured for attachment to the fixing pin of an external fixator apparatus. External fixators are commonly used orthopedic devices that stabilize broken bones using pins or wires connected to an external frame, and this invention leverages that existing infrastructure to deliver therapeutic benefits.

The device body incorporates one or more light source units strategically positioned to emit therapeutic light directly onto the patient's skin surface surrounding the fixation site. This configuration allows for continuous or intermittent light therapy to be administered precisely where it is needed most—at the location of the fracture and surrounding tissue—without requiring additional invasive procedures or separate device attachment points. The integration with the existing external fixator hardware means that patients undergoing fracture stabilization can simultaneously receive photobiomodulation therapy, potentially reducing healing time, decreasing inflammation, and improving overall tissue regeneration at the wound site.

### Second Embodiment: Insertable Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

In another aspect of the invention, an insertable device is provided for direct application to osteomyelitis-affected bone tissue. This device features multiple light-emitting members that are spatially distributed along its structure, allowing for broader coverage of infected bone areas compared to single-point light sources.

A key innovative feature of this embodiment is its adaptability: the device is constructed such that it can be cut or bent by the treating physician to conform precisely to the specific anatomical dimensions and contours of the osteomyelitis site. This customization capability addresses a critical limitation of standard medical devices, which often come in fixed configurations that may not adequately match the irregular geometries typically presented by bone infections. By enabling physicians to modify the device's shape and length according to the specific clinical presentation, the invention ensures optimal contact and light delivery regardless of the infection's location, size, or shape within the bone structure.

## Detailed Description

### Light Source Configuration and Therapeutic Mechanism

The light source units employed in both embodiments of this invention are selected and configured to emit wavelengths known to promote therapeutic effects, including antimicrobial action against infection-causing bacteria, enhanced cellular metabolism, increased blood circulation, and stimulation of tissue repair mechanisms. The specific wavelength ranges may be optimized depending on whether the primary therapeutic goal is wound healing acceleration, antibacterial action against osteomyelitis-causing pathogens, or a combination of both therapeutic effects.

### Attachment and Positioning Mechanisms

The external fixator-attachable embodiment includes mounting mechanisms compatible with standard external fixator pin diameters and configurations, ensuring broad applicability across different fixator systems currently used in clinical practice. This attachment system is designed to maintain stable positioning of the light source units throughout the treatment period, even as patients move or the external fixator undergoes routine adjustments.

### Customizable Design for Osteomyelitis Treatment

The insertable device's cuttable and bendable properties are achieved through material selection and structural design that maintains functional integrity of the light-emitting members even after modification. This ensures that regardless of how the device is customized during surgical placement, each light-emitting member continues to function properly, delivering consistent therapeutic light output to the surrounding infected bone tissue.

The spaced arrangement of light-emitting members along the device's length allows for even distribution of therapeutic light across the entire affected area, rather than concentrating treatment at a single point. This design consideration is particularly important for osteomyelitis cases, which often involve infection spreading along bone marrow cavities or affecting extended regions of bone tissue.

## Advantages of the Invention

This invention offers several significant advantages over existing treatment modalities:

1. **Targeted Delivery**: By positioning light sources directly at fracture sites or within infected bone areas, the invention ensures therapeutic light reaches the precise location where healing or antimicrobial action is needed most.

2. **Customization and Adaptability**: The cuttable and bendable nature of the insertable device allows for patient-specific customization, accommodating the wide variation in osteomyelitis presentation across different patients and anatomical locations.

3. **Integration with Existing Treatment Protocols**: The external fixator-compatible embodiment allows for phototherapy to be incorporated into standard fracture treatment protocols without requiring significant additional procedures.

4. **Enhanced Healing Outcomes**: By combining mechanical stabilization (via external fixators) or direct bone access (via insertable devices) with targeted phototherapy, this invention has the potential to accelerate healing timelines and improve treatment outcomes for patients suffering from complex fractures and bone infections.

5. **Reduced Treatment Burden**: Consolidating fracture stabilization and light therapy delivery into a single device system may reduce the overall treatment burden on patients, minimizing the need for separate therapeutic interventions.

## Conclusion

This invention represents a significant advancement in the field of orthopedic and infectious disease treatment by providing medical devices capable of delivering targeted, customizable light therapy directly to fracture sites and osteomyelitis-affected bone tissue. Through the dual embodiments described—the external fixator-attachable device and the insertable, customizable light-emitting device—this invention offers healthcare providers powerful new tools for accelerating wound healing and combating persistent bone infections, ultimately improving patient outcomes in complex orthopedic cases.

# Patent Abstract

**Title:** External Fixator Pin Assembly with Integrated Phototherapy Module for Enhanced Pin-Site and Fracture Healing

**Abstract:**

A medical device system integrating light-based therapy with external fixation hardware for orthopedic trauma management is disclosed. The device comprises an external fixator pin having a conventional bone-engaging threaded shaft and an integrated or attachable phototherapy module positioned at or near the skin-penetration site. The phototherapy module houses one or more light-emitting diodes (LEDs) or low-level laser sources configured to deliver therapeutic wavelengths, typically in the red (600-700 nm) and near-infrared (700-1000 nm) spectrum, to surrounding soft tissue and the underlying bone-pin interface.

The module may be configured as a removable collar or sleeve that clamps onto the external portion of a standard fixator pin, or as a factory-integrated component of a novel pin design, allowing compatibility with existing fixation frames. An onboard or externally connected microcontroller regulates light dosage, pulse frequency, and treatment duration according to programmable therapeutic protocols, with optional wireless connectivity for remote monitoring and adjustment by clinicians. A power source, such as a rechargeable battery or inductive charging coil, supplies energy to the light-emitting elements, while a biocompatible, sterilizable housing protects the electronic components from bodily fluids and external contamination.

The device is intended to reduce the incidence of pin-site infections, decrease localized inflammation, and accelerate osseous and soft tissue healing through photobiomodulation effects at the fracture site. Additional embodiments may incorporate sensors for temperature, impedance, or infection biomarkers to provide real-time feedback and adaptive therapy adjustment. This integration of phototherapy directly at the site of external fixation offers a novel, minimally invasive means of improving clinical outcomes for patients undergoing fracture stabilization, potentially reducing healing time, complication rates, and the need for adjunctive treatments.

---

*Note: This is a draft template for illustrative purposes. Actual patent filings require consultation with a registered patent attorney or agent to ensure proper legal claims, prior art review, and compliance with USPTO or relevant patent office requirements.*

# TECHNICAL DISCLOSURE

## Integrated Phototherapeutic System for External Fixation and Intramedullary Infection Control

---

## 1. FIELD OF THE INVENTION

This disclosure relates to therapeutic light-delivery devices for orthopedic applications, specifically: (A) a photobiomodulation (PBM) module integrated into external fixator hardware for accelerating soft tissue and bone healing at pin/wire sites and fracture zones, and (B) an insertable fiber-optic probe device for localized phototherapeutic and photodynamic treatment of osteomyelitis within the medullary canal or infected bone cavity. The two devices are disclosed together as complementary components of a staged treatment system for patients with open fractures, external fixation, and associated risk of or established bone infection.

---

## 2. BACKGROUND

Open fractures and complex trauma frequently require external fixation, in which percutaneous pins or wires anchor a rigid external frame to stabilized bone segments. Two persistent clinical problems arise in this population:

1. **Delayed soft tissue and bone healing**, compounded by pin-site friction, micromotion, and compromised local vascularity, which prolongs frame duration and increases infection risk.
2. **Osteomyelitis**, a bone infection with biofilm-protected bacterial colonies that resist systemic antibiotics due to poor penetration into avascular or necrotic bone, often requiring prolonged IV antibiotic courses, surgical debridement, and antibiotic-loaded cement spacers.

Photobiomodulation (low-level light therapy, wavelengths ~600–950 nm) has documented effects on fibroblast proliferation, collagen synthesis, angiogenesis, and reduction of inflammatory cytokines. Separately, antimicrobial blue light (405–470 nm) and photodynamic therapy (light-activated photosensitizer chemistry, typically 630–690 nm) have demonstrated bactericidal activity, including against biofilm-embedded and antibiotic-resistant organisms, without the resistance mechanisms associated with antibiotics.

Current clinical practice does not integrate light delivery into fixation hardware, nor does it provide a controlled means of delivering therapeutic or antimicrobial light directly into infected medullary bone without extensive surgical exposure. This disclosure addresses both gaps with two devices sharing a common control architecture.

---

## 3. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

**Device A — External Fixator-Integrated Phototherapy Module ("Fixator-PBM")**
A modular array of light-emitting elements mechanically coupled to standard external fixator rails/rings, positioned to irradiate pin-skin interfaces and the underlying fracture zone transcutaneously. The module is removable, sterilizable, adjustable along the fixator rails, and driven by a programmable controller delivering defined wavelength, irradiance, and duty-cycle protocols.

**Device B — Insertable Osteomyelitis Light-Emitting Probe ("Osteo-Probe")**
A slender, flexible or semi-rigid fiber-optic probe designed for insertion through a percutaneous tract, cannulated screw, or surgical debridement window into the medullary canal or bone abscess cavity. The probe delivers antimicrobial and/or photodynamic-activating light directly to infected bone tissue, optionally combined with a co-administered photosensitizer and/or an integrated irrigation/aspiration lumen and thermal sensor for safety monitoring.

**Combined System**
Both devices interface with a shared base control console containing light source drivers, dosimetry software, treatment logging, and safety interlocks. The console can operate Device A prophylactically during the fixation period and, if osteomyelitis develops or is anticipated (e.g., contaminated open fracture, Gustilo-Anderson Type IIIB/C), can be switched to drive Device B during the same admission using the same power/control unit, providing a continuum of phototherapeutic care.

---

## 4. DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### 4.1 Device A: External Fixator Phototherapy Module

**4.1.1 Mechanical Architecture**
- A set of clip-on or ring-clamp carriers ("light pods") sized to attach to standard fixator rail diameters (4–11 mm) and ring/half-ring fixator systems (e.g., circular/Ilizarov-type frames).
- Each light pod houses a small PCB array of LEDs or low-power laser diodes, encapsulated in a sterilizable, autoclavable, or single-use disposable optical window (medical-grade silicone or polycarbonate).
- Pods are repositionable along the rail via a toothed or friction-lock track, allowing alignment over each pin/wire site regardless of patient-specific frame configuration.
- A flexible, gooseneck or hinged arm permits angular adjustment so the emission surface can be oriented perpendicular to the skin at each pin site, standoff distance maintained at 1–2 cm via a spacer collar.

**4.1.2 Optical Specification**
- Dual-wavelength emission: 660 nm (red, superficial dermal/epidermal effect at pin-skin interface) and 850 nm (near-infrared, deeper penetration toward periosteum/bone).
- Irradiance: 5–50 mW/cm² at target surface, adjustable.
- Energy dose: programmable fluence 2–10 J/cm² per site per session, consistent with published PBM protocols for wound healing.
- Pulsed or continuous-wave operation, pulse frequency 2–1000 Hz selectable, to modulate depth of effect and reduce thermal load.

**4.1.3 Control and Power**
- Each pod connects via low-voltage ribbon cable to a beltpack or frame-mounted control unit containing rechargeable battery, microcontroller, and treatment-timer.
- Preset protocols selectable by clinician (e.g., "Acute Pin Site — 5 min BID," "Delayed Union — 10 min QD").
- Onboard sensors: contact/proximity sensor to confirm pod is seated against skin (prevents inadvertent operation in free space), and skin-surface thermistor with automatic shutoff above 40°C.
- Optional Bluetooth/telemetry link for logging dose, compliance, and adherence data to an EMR-connected app.

**4.1.4 Additional Embodiments**
- A conformal flexible light sheet wrapping partially around the limb circumference between rail segments for broader-field irradiation of soft tissue, in addition to discrete pin-site pods.
- Interchangeable pod modules permitting swap between PBM wavelengths and antimicrobial blue-light (405 nm) wavelength for pin-site infection prophylaxis.
- Frame-integrated design in which LED elements are embedded directly into a proprietary fixator rail during manufacture, eliminating the need for clip-on pods.

### 4.2 Device B: Insertable Osteomyelitis Probe

**4.2.1 Mechanical Architecture**
- A flexible fiber-optic probe (diameter 1.0–2.5 mm) with a side-firing or diffusing-tip distal segment (length 5–30 mm) to distribute light circumferentially within a medullary canal or cavity rather than as a forward-focused beam, reducing local hot-spots.
- Compatible delivery routes:
 (a) via a cannulated fixator pin/screw with a hollow bore permitting probe advancement directly to the bone-pin interface;
 (b) via a percutaneous introducer sheath/trocar placed under fluoroscopic guidance into a debrided abscess cavity or intramedullary canal;
 (c) via an existing sinus tract in chronic draining osteomyelitis.
- Optional coaxial lumen for saline irrigation and/or aspiration of purulent material, and a separate lumen for local instillation of a photosensitizer solution (e.g., methylene blue or a porphyrin-based agent) prior to activation.
- Radiopaque marker band at the distal tip for fluoroscopic/CT confirmation of placement depth.
- Integrated micro-thermocouple at the tip for real-time temperature feedback (bone tissue thermal injury threshold considerations).

**4.2.2 Optical Specification**
- Selectable wavelength modes:
 - **Antimicrobial blue-light mode**: 405–470 nm, direct bactericidal effect via endogenous porphyrin photoexcitation in bacteria (including MRSA and biofilm-embedded organisms), irradiance

# INVENTION SUMMARY

## Title of Invention
**PHOTOTHERAPY APPARATUS FOR USE WITH ORTHOPEDIC EXTERNAL FIXATION SYSTEMS AND METHOD FOR INTRAOSSEOUS PHOTOBIOMODULATION IN THE TREATMENT OF OSTEOMYELITIS**

---

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to medical devices for orthopedic trauma and reconstructive surgery, and more particularly to a phototherapy delivery system configured for integration with external fixation hardware (e.g., ring fixators, monolateral rail systems, hybrid frames) to deliver photobiomodulation (PBM) therapy to bone, soft tissue, and pin/wire tract sites. The invention further relates to a specialized intraosseous variant configured for direct insertion into medullary or cortical bone defects for the localized treatment of osteomyelitis and infected non-unions.

---

## Background of the Invention

External fixation is a widely used technique for the stabilization of complex fractures, limb lengthening, and correction of deformities, as well as for management of infected bone (e.g., via the Ilizarov method). Pin tract infections, delayed union, non-union, and chronic osteomyelitis remain significant complications associated with prolonged external fixation.

Photobiomodulation therapy, utilizing low-level laser light or specific wavelength LED sources (typically in the red to near-infrared spectrum, approximately 600–1000 nm), has been shown in clinical literature to promote osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and reduction of inflammatory markers, as well as to exert bactericidal or bacteriostatic effects when combined with photosensitizing agents (antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, aPDT).

However, no device currently exists that (a) structurally integrates with standard external fixator hardware to enable repeatable, positionally-stable delivery of phototherapy to fracture sites and pin tracts without disassembly of the fixation frame, and (b) provides a sterile, minimally invasive means of delivering light energy directly into infected medullary bone via a fixator pin channel or dedicated osteotomy port. There exists an unmet need for such a system.

---

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a **modular phototherapy apparatus** comprising:

1. **A Fixator-Mounted Photoemitter Array Unit (PAU)** — a clamp-on or rail-mounted housing containing an array of LED and/or laser diode emitters, configured to attach directly to the rings, rods, or rails of an external fixator frame via a quick-release coupling compatible with standard fixator clamp geometries (e.g., Ilizarov ring bores, Taylor Spatial Frame struts, or monolateral rail dovetails).

2. **A Percutaneous Pin-Sleeve Light Guide (PSLG)** — an optically clear or fiber-coupled sleeve that surrounds a standard fixator pin or wire at the skin entry point, channeling light from the PAU along the pin tract to reduce pin-site infection and promote peri-pin osseointegration.

3. **An Intraosseous Phototherapy Probe (IPP)** — *[the osteomyelitis-specific variant, detailed below]* — a sterilizable, cannulated or solid-core fiber-optic probe dimensioned for insertion through a fixator pin channel, corticotomy, or dedicated drill port directly into the medullary canal or a debrided osteomyelitic cavity, delivering light energy at the infection site.

4. **A Control and Power Console** — an external, battery- or mains-powered unit housing the laser/LED driver electronics, dosimetry control (wavelength selection, irradiance, pulse frequency, treatment duration), safety interlocks (thermal cutoff, tissue-contact sensing), and optionally, real-time temperature feedback via integrated thermocouple or fiber Bragg grating sensor.

5. **Optional Photosensitizer Delivery Adjunct** — a coaxial micro-channel or catheter lumen integrated into the IPP for local instillation of a photosensitizing agent (e.g., methylene blue, toluidine blue O, or indocyanine green) prior to activation, enabling antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) in situ.

---

## Detailed Description of Preferred Embodiments

### A. External (Frame-Mounted) Embodiment

The PAU comprises a rigid or semi-rigid housing containing between 4 and 64 individually addressable LED or laser diode emitters, arranged in a planar, arcuate, or annular configuration to conform to the geometry of the external fixator ring or rail. The housing incorporates:

- A **universal coupling mechanism** (spring-loaded clamp, dovetail slide, or threaded post) compatible with common fixator hardware interfaces;
- **Adjustable standoff arms** permitting variable distance and angulation between the emitter array and the skin surface to accommodate soft tissue swelling;
- A **flexible circuit substrate** allowing the array to conform to curved ring geometries;
- **Wavelength-selectable emitter banks**, e.g., 660 nm (red, superficial soft tissue/anti-inflammatory), 810–850 nm (near-infrared, deeper penetration to bone), and optionally 405 nm (violet, direct antibacterial effect) emitters, selectable via the control console;
- An **optical shielding collar** to prevent stray irradiation of non-target tissue and to protect operator/patient eyes.

The PSLG comprises a short (1–3 cm) biocompatible, autoclavable sleeve of medical-grade fluoropolymer or sapphire-doped silica, sized to snugly encircle a 1.5–6.0 mm diameter fixator pin or wire at its skin-entry point. The sleeve is optically coupled to the PAU via a flexible fiber-optic pigtail, permitting light delivery concentrated at the pin-skin interface — a site of elevated infection risk — without requiring removal or loosening of the pin.

### B. Intraosseous (Osteomyelitis) Embodiment — Key Novel Variant

The **Intraosseous Phototherapy Probe (IPP)** is specifically configured for direct placement within infected or debrided bone and represents the principal inventive advance for osteomyelitis management. Preferred features include:

1. **Cannulated Trocar-Tipped Shaft**: A rigid or semi-flexible shaft (outer diameter 1.8–4.5 mm) fabricated from surgical-grade stainless steel, titanium, or PEEK, with a sharpened or trocar-style distal tip enabling direct percutaneous or intraoperative insertion through:
   - an existing external fixator pin channel (post pin removal),
   - a dedicated drill hole,
   - or an open debridement/corticotomy site.

2. **Distal Diffusing Optical Tip**: A cylindrical light-diffusing fiber segment (5–40 mm active length, selectable per defect size) at the distal end of the shaft, engineered via micro-etched scattering centers or a diffusing sleeve to emit light radially (360°) or in a directional side-firing pattern along the medullary canal or debrided cavity, ensuring homogeneous irradiance of the endosteal surface and cavity walls.

3. **Dual-Lumen Configuration**: An inner optical fiber lumen for light transmission and an outer coaxial lumen enabling:
   - irrigation/aspiration of the medullary canal,
   - local antibiotic or photosensitizer instillation,
   - and/or biopsy/culture sampling — permitting combined diagnostic and therapeutic use in a single instrument.

4. **Depth-Indexed Sterile Sheath**: A graduated, radiopaque, single-use outer sheath permitting fluoroscopic confirmation of insertion depth and preventing tissue trauma or fiber contamination during placement/withdrawal.

5. **Docking Interface to External Fixator**: A proximal fitting enabling the IPP to be mechanically indexed to the external fixator frame itself (via the same clamp used for the pin it replaces), maintaining stable, reproducible positioning across multiple treatment sessions without repeat imaging, and permitting the probe to be left indwelling (capped) between treatment sessions if clinically indicated, with only the fiber-optic connector exposed externally for reconnection to the console.

6. **Thermal and Dosimetric Safety Feedback**: A micro-thermocouple or fiber Bragg grating sensor integrated adjacent to the diffusing tip, feeding real-time temperature data to the control console to prevent thermal necrosis of adjacent healthy bone, with automatic power modulation or shutoff above a preset threshold (e.g., 43°C).

7. **Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy (aPDT) Mode**: In a further variant, the outer coaxial lumen delivers a photosensitizing dye directly to the infected medullary space prior to laser activation (typically 630–670 nm for methylene blue/toluidine blue activation), producing reactive oxygen species locally toxic to biofilm-embedded pathogens (e.g., *Staphylococcus aureus*, including MRSA, and *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*) while sparing systemic exposure.

### C. Control Console

The console provides:
- Multi-channel independent control of PAU and IPP emitters;
- Programmable treatment protocols (continuous wave or pulsed, 1–500 Hz);
- Dose logging (J/cm²) with automatic energy calculation based on emitter count, wavelength, and treatment duration;
- Wireless telemetry for integration with electronic health records;
- Safety interlocks including tissue-contact/insertion-depth verification and automatic shutdown upon probe disconnection or thermal excursion.

# Patent Abstract

**Title:** Photobiomodulation Device for Wound Healing at Skeletal Fixator Pin Sites and Modular Light-Emitting Insert for Osteomyelitis Treatment

## Abstract

A medical light therapy device is disclosed for promoting wound healing at percutaneous pin sites associated with external skeletal fixators, and for treating osteomyelitis via an implantable or insertable modular light-emitting apparatus. In one embodiment, the device comprises a clip-on or collar-style housing configured to attach directly to a skeletal fixator pin proximal to the skin penetration site, the housing containing one or more light-emitting elements oriented to deliver therapeutic wavelengths (e.g., red and near-infrared light) circumferentially or directionally toward the pin-skin interface to reduce infection risk, inflammation, and promote soft tissue and osseous healing.

In a related embodiment, an elongated flexible insert is provided for treatment of osteomyelitis within bone canals, cavities, or surgical sites, comprising a plurality of discrete segments arranged in series along a flexible substrate, each segment housing one or more light-emitting diodes or laser diodes powered via an integrated or externally coupled power source. The segments are separated by designated cut lines or perforations, enabling a clinician to trim the insert to a patient-specific length while preserving functional independence of remaining segments and electrical continuity of the truncated assembly. The modular design allows adjustable placement within irregular or variably sized bone defects, delivering localized photobiomodulation therapy to infected or compromised bone tissue.

Both embodiments may include wavelength-selectable emitters, programmable pulsing controllers, dosimetry sensors, and biocompatible encapsulation suitable for sustained contact with skin or implantation adjacent to bone tissue. The invention provides a minimally invasive, adaptable platform for enhancing healing outcomes in orthopedic trauma and infection management.
